trajectory_summary: This is a short, procedurally clean setter call: the rep moves through verify items efficiently, captures the bill live on the call, and locks a specific day and time. Energy stays roughly flat rather than building — the customer's repeated cost questions are deferred correctly but never resolved, leaving mild residual curiosity rather than excitement heading into the closer call.

observed_outcome.quote: Got you down for, Wednesday next Wednesday, the, twenty ninth at 10:30. And, yeah, we'll see you then.
observed_outcome.reasoning: A specific day (Wednesday the 29th) and time (10:30) were confirmed verbally and the bill was captured live via text, meeting the criteria for a booked outcome; however the disclosed co-owner was never confirmed for the appointment.

bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: The rep captures the bill figure and even gets a spontaneous escalation cue from the customer ('That that will go up'), but never turns the number into an explicit reason to act — no callback to the $145 figure occurs when reiterating the program pitch or at button-up.

interest_reason_audit.reasoning: The rep never explicitly asked what interested Lauren in solar; the call opens by confirming the request came in ('I just got a request here') rather than probing her personal motivation, so no reason was ever surfaced to reinforce later.

primary_coaching_focus.quote: There is. And anyone who makes the decisions.
primary_coaching_focus.why: A second decision-maker is disclosed on the title and never named, probed, or invited to the appointment — this is the single highest-risk gap on the call because it leaves the booked appointment structurally vulnerable per protocols.spouse_decision.

key_moments.quote: I would definitely say those trees on the side of your home, might be causing them mostly.
key_moments.stewart_read: Rep guesses at which side of the house the shading trees are on before actually checking, then has to be corrected twice by the customer (left/right, front-facing orientation). This is an improvised technical claim rather than an admitted gap.

key_moments.quote: Yeah. So our goal here is to swap out your electric bill with your current utility provider and replace that with a cheaper solar payment.
key_moments.stewart_read: This is the natural landing spot for the bill-as-villain reframe — rep states the swap concept but never ties it back to her actual bill pain, which arrives just one minute later at 04:02.

key_moments.quote: What can I expect for the cheaper payment?
key_moments.stewart_read: Second touch of the cost-curiosity pattern; customer directly asks for a number and the rep defers to the specialist rather than using her own bill pain as the answer.

key_moments.quote: Yeah. So there's multiple options you can look at, and, I would definitely bring that up to the specialist because I'm not a 100% versed on on all the options that we offer.
key_moments.stewart_read: Rep admits the knowledge gap directly and routes to the specialist rather than guessing — this is correct scope discipline, not creep, and stands in useful contrast to the earlier improvised tree-orientation answer.
